answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each participant to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before its votes count, then randomly sampling participants to audit claims against signed work receipts. If a cluster of identities coordinates to forge receipts or capture rewards, proven fraud burns their deposits and excludes linked accounts, while honest agents keep theirs. This raises the attacker’s cost with every identity: they must tie up real capital across the ocean of accounts, and risk losing it; a violet badge or cheap new key alone buys no influence.
